description: God told Israel the sacrifices were never the point. What He wanted was them. It is still easy to substitute activity for relationship.
excerpt: Activity gives us something to measure. Sacrifices could be counted. Boxes could be checked. At the end of the day, they had something to point to. Relationship is harder to measure.
verse: "When I led your ancestors out of Egypt, it was not burnt offerings and sacrifices I wanted from them."
body_html:
At first glance this verse can be confusing. Especially if you are going to just pick out one verse. God did ask for sacrifices. The whole Old Testament sacrificial system was set up by Him. So what does He mean it wasn't what He wanted?

The next verse fills it in. God says what He actually wanted was for them to obey Him, to be His people, and for Him to be their God. The sacrifices were there, but they were never the point. The relationship was.

It's easy to substitute activity for relationship.

Activity gives us something to measure. Sacrifices could be counted. Boxes could be checked. At the end of the day, they had something to point to. Relationship is harder to measure. There's no scoreboard, no progress bar, just the slow work of actually knowing Him and being known.

So we drift toward the activity. It's easier. It feels productive. And it lets us feel spiritual without ever actually drawing close.

Israel did the same thing. They kept up the sacrifices while their hearts were far from God. They went through the motions of the ritual while ignoring the God the ritual was pointing to. And God had to say it plainly. This was never what I wanted from you.

He wanted them. He wanted to be their God, for them to be His people, for the whole thing to be about relationship instead of ritual.

And it's the same today. He doesn't want our checklists or a track record of showing up. He doesn't want the version of us that reads the plan, sings the songs, and posts the verse without ever letting Him into our real life.

He wants us.

Where have you been substituting activity for relationship with God?
question: Where have you been substituting activity for relationship with God?
